record_type: Translated inherited original image-inspection observations; no images included
scope: Six Applied PDF pages, four PRX figures, and seven Research figures; page and figure units are not interchangeable. Not a 300- or 700-paper image audit.

records.visual_observation: Actual image inspection: five design rows by four physical-observable columns preserve the same within-column axes; labels sit beside y-axes and centered below each plot. Small inset parameter summaries carry useful content but must remain legible at final width.
records.visual_limitation: Do not copy its20-panel density without comparable necessity; row/column invariants make the density interpretable.

records.visual_observation: Actual image inspection: a compact six-panel device-physics figure combines level diagram, event histogram, gate map, fidelity and relaxation traces. Insets show the pulse that generates each measurement; color and marker shapes connect selected operating points across panels.
records.visual_limitation: One-column typesetting makes inset labels small; check final-size readability rather than using this as a minimum text-size precedent.

records.visual_observation: Actual image inspection: a dense proposed optical setup explicitly connects spectral branches, fiber delays, detection, feedforward electronics and two output arms. A small line-color key encodes different optical/electrical media; device abbreviations are expanded in the caption.
records.visual_limitation: This is a proposed system, not a fully realized demonstration. Several long loops and crossings increase tracing effort; reuse functional grouping/dependency detail rather than its exact routing or color-only distinctions.

records.visual_observation: Actual image inspection: conductance-map input, transformer, parameter correction, updated Hamiltonian/maps and loss form a closed scientific feedback graph. Black and blue arrows distinguish training and inference in a single-column area.
records.visual_limitation: Training/inference meaning should also have text or line-style cues for accessibility; this figure alone does not establish experimental closure of the loop.

records.visual_observation: Actual image inspection: simulation and experimental gain maps form aligned comparison columns with cable-length annotations spanning corresponding rows; upper color bars share the gain scale. Shared lower frequency labels and a left shared voltage-bias label reduce repetition. Right-hand performance panels separate gain/noise from saturation.
records.visual_limitation: Two cable lengths also use different bias/current settings, so visual alignment is a mechanism comparison, not an all-other-variables-fixed claim. Dual y-axes require explicit units and curve mapping.

records.visual_observation: Actual image inspection: three parallel pipelines compare the order of parameter assignment, expensive operator construction, evaluation and error mitigation. Consistent operation colors plus explicit mathematical labels permit step-by-step comparison; arrows encode dependency rather than decoration.
records.visual_limitation: The transferable element is operation ordering and reused work, not a universal three-column template or the specific palette.

figures.observation: Architecture, the measured array, and predicted performance occupy separate regions; axis titles sit near their axes.
Each optical component aligns with a sensitivity plot below it, connecting structure to diagnostics.
Location lines connect images above to shared-x quantitative plots below; a model at the right connects back to the structure. Colors distinguish radial groups and metrics.

records.scope: Only the listed figures were visually inspected; not a complete-figure audit of the paper or corpus.

figures.observation: Group conditions and formulas form inputs, parallel constraints, criteria, and outputs, with dashed grouping, thin connections, and limited semantic color.

records.scope: Only the listed figures were visually inspected; not a complete-figure audit of the paper or corpus.

records.observation: Chip grid, circuit, DAG, mapping, and encoding tables align within one figure. Region colors remain consistent across objects, blue arrows show transformations, and the caption explains an encoding example.
records.transfer: When the contribution is a representation, show one instance across representations rather than only generic input/algorithm/output boxes.
records.caution: Redundant position, numbering, or text should supplement color. This is not a journal-wide workflow template.
records.scope: Only the listed figures and visible captions on that page; not a complete-image audit.

records.observation: A left column connects structure, density, discretization, QUBO, solving, and coordinate output; the right column supplies matching molecular, density, and grid examples. Dashed boxes mark the solver boundary.
records.transfer: Distinguish scientific-object transformations from computational-module boundaries and place intermediate results beside the corresponding step.
records.caution: A commercial logo is only part of the example, not a substitute for methods or resource budgets; unnecessary whitespace can be reduced.
records.scope: Only the listed figures and visible captions on that page; not a complete-image audit.

records.observation: Figure 2 uses a fixed graph layout across four stages; node colors mark selected, removed, and remaining nodes. Local highlighting identifies a node that restarts reduction. Figure 3 distinguishes algorithms with shape and color and includes a hard-instance inset.
records.transfer: Keep object coordinates fixed across mechanism stages and mark the local change; retain comparable baselines and uncertainties in data plots.
records.caution: Exact reduction and heuristic node selection have different guarantees; a continuous visual workflow does not merge those guarantees.
records.scope: Only the listed figures and visible captions on that page; not a complete-image audit.

records.observation: Figure 3 arranges raw T1, a binned close-up, and converted quality factor in three columns. Dashed lines link regions and a secondary axis records counts. Figure 4 compares device and process distributions with separate mean, median, and quartile encodings.
records.transfer: When processing changes the comparison, connect the raw quantity, estimation steps, and final metric in a traceable figure sequence.
records.caution: A dual axis is used only for clearly labeled different quantities here; this is not general advice to prefer dual axes.
records.scope: Only the listed figures and visible captions on that page; not a complete-image audit.

records.observation: Frequency and intensity noise occupy two rows; response functions, PSD, and error contribution occupy three columns. Arrows connect input spectra to contributions and shared column labels reduce repetition.
records.transfer: Use repeated panel organization for the same calculation, allowing readers to connect response times spectrum to error sources.
records.caution: The pale PSD color has weak contrast when reduced; borrow the structure rather than the exact palette and check final-size readability.
